claims.text: Bulbapedia records Pokemon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! as a Japan-only Game Boy Color title released on March 28, 2001.
Bulbapedia describes the game as a Game Boy Color sequel to Pokemon Trading Card Game, developed by Hudson Soft and published by The Pokemon Company.
Bulbapedia states copies of the game included Team GR's Mewtwo and Lugia promotional cards; PokeBoon also describes Great Rocket's Mewtwo and Lugia as Pokemon Card GB2 included promos.
The local release family models one row: Team GR's Mewtwo source index 227, with the promotion note Pokemon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR! insert.

The game's story centers on Team Great Rocket, GR Island, kidnapped Club Masters, and stolen Legendary Cards, making the included Mewtwo an object from the sequel's villain architecture rather than a generic Mewtwo promo.
Bulbapedia lists Shin-ichi Yoshida / 吉田振一 as a Pokemon TCG illustrator with Rocket, Dark, Neo, e-Card, VS, Vending, and unnumbered-promo credits, including Team GR's Mewtwo.

The GB2 insert route matters because it binds a physical card to a playable digital TCG sequel: the card is not only a promo, but a bridge between cartridge, villain campaign, in-game card logic, and old-back collecting.
This release dossier carries a special identification packet for the Pokemon Card GB2 Team GR's Mewtwo source-row boundary.

narrative.human_title: Pokemon Card GB2 — Team GR's Mewtwo as cartridge-born villain myth
narrative.why_it_matters: This is one of the places where Pokemon's assembly becomes wonderfully literal: a Game Boy Color cartridge ships with a real card, and the real card points back at the digital villain world. Team GR's Mewtwo is Mewtwo pulled through Team Great Rocket's machinery, stamped with a GB route, paired with Lugia in the game box, and drawn by Shin-ichi Yoshida, whose Rocket/Dark work already knew how to make power look dangerous. It is a pocket-sized hinge between software, cardboard, and villain lore.

claims.text: The local catalog anchors Team GR's Mewtwo as source index 227 in the Pokemon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR insert source row.
Bulbapedia identifies the card as Team GR's Mewtwo / GR団のミュウツー, a Psychic-type Basic Pokemon card with HP 70, LV.35, No. 150, and an official-tournament-use restriction.
Bulbapedia lists the physical print's Pokemon Power as Dark Wave / わるいはどう and its attack as Dark Amplification / わるいぞうふく, with a related but distinct in-game print text.
Bulbapedia and PokeBoon identify Shin-ichi Yoshida / 吉田振一 as the illustrator for Team GR's Mewtwo.
Bulbapedia states the card has a GB symbol in place of an expansion symbol, referencing its ties to Pokemon Trading Card Game 2.
The card was available as an unnumbered promotional card alongside Lugia in copies of Pokemon Trading Card Game 2: The Invasion of Team GR!, released for Game Boy Color on March 28, 2001.
Yoshida's TCG credits include Rocket's Mewtwo, Rocket's Zapdos, Dark Weezing, Dark Tyranitar, and Team GR's Mewtwo, giving this promo a visible Rocket/Dark visual lineage.

Team GR's Mewtwo matters because it is a physical villain-card artifact from a Japan-only digital sequel: a Mewtwo tied simultaneously to cartridge history, Team Great Rocket story, pack-in collecting, and old-back promo identity.

narrative.human_title: Team GR's Mewtwo — source index 227, the GB villain card
narrative.why_it_matters: Team GR's Mewtwo feels like it should hum when you hold it. It is Mewtwo filtered through Team Great Rocket, through a Japan-only Game Boy Color sequel, through a GB symbol where an expansion mark would usually sit, and through Shin-ichi Yoshida's dark-card vocabulary. The card is not just powerful-looking; it is a little receipt from a moment when Pokemon let the video game and the TCG fold into each other.
